architecturalAnswer: The host ABI is not one uniform authorization boundary: the 41 in-scope raw env/filesystem/SQLite primitives are deliberately below caller-side typed authorization (or are used only by explicit unarmed/diagnostic paths), while four module-resolution ABI functions call typed Host resolvers from inside their ABI bodies and therefore remain correctly seeded. The native-op layer is the real package-principal decision surface for process.env, filesystem, and SQLite.

representativeFlows.finding: __exactGetAllEnv authorizes each exact compiled key before getEnvValue enters ex_host_env_get. The ABI itself only reads compiled/ambient state. __exactGetEnv likewise makes the typed decision at src/engine/hermes_runtime.cc:4977; an armed scalar read returns the principal overlay rather than ambient host state.

The JavaScript read reaches __exactFsRead. Armed Windows execution takes the typed private-VFS path; ex_host_fs_read/ex_host_fs_pread are reached only by the unarmed compatibility branch after its legacy retained-entry check. The raw ABI body performs I/O, not authorization. POSIX whole-file read/write has the same split at src/engine/hermes_runtime_fs.cc:5059-5215.

__exactSqliteOpen authorizes and opens an armed descriptor before ex_host_sqlite_open_checked_fd; retained statements repeat requireSqliteAuthorization before calling raw ex_host_sqlite_* functions. The rusqlite ABI bodies have no typed decision.

correctlySeededComparison.finding: This surface really performs exact-name typed decisions and remains an obligation.
